paper.title_en: Impact of Dipolar and Antisymmetric Interactions on Quantum Correlations in a Mixed-Spin Two-Site System
paper.abstract_en: In this work, we investigate the quantum correlations of a hybrid-spin (1/2, 1) system governed by an XXZ Hamiltonian that incorporates both a dipolar coupling and the antisymmetric Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction. By determining the full energy spectrum and constructing the corresponding thermal density matrix, we systematically analyze how entanglement, quantum coherence, and measurement-induced disturbance evolve under the combined influence of interaction parameters and temperature. Our results reveal a clear hierarchy of robustness: while entanglement is highly sensitive to thermal fluctuations, measurement-induced disturbance and coherence persist over a considerably broader range, demonstrating their superior resilience. Moreover, by extending the comparison to the two-qubit framework, we show that the restricted Hilbert space of the latter amplifies the effects of both dipolar and Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interactions, leading to abrupt changes in entanglement due to the direct mixing between singlet and triplet states. In contrast, the qubit-qutrit system benefits from the additional magnetic sublevels of the spin-1 particle, which open multiple transition pathways and redistribute quantum correlations across an enlarged Hilbert space, thereby producing a smoother and less fragile dynamical response. Taken together, these observations provide a unified perspective on the complementary roles played by dipolar and Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya couplings in shaping the behavior of quantum correlations and highlight the potential of mixed-spin architectures for achieving enhanced stability in thermally noisy environments.
